title: self-update fails on a platform-incomplete latest release instead of falling back to the newest release with a matching asset
description:
Self-update fails outright when the newest release has no asset for the running platform, instead of falling back to the newest release that does. A node can be blocked from updating at all while a perfectly good build sits one tag back.

Observed on helsinki, 2026-07-30T09:17Z:

    cara self-update run
    cara self_update_failed: release v0.0.42 has no asset cara-0.0.42-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
    (available: ["cara-0.0.42-aarch64-darwin.sha256", "cara-0.0.42-aarch64-darwin.tar.gz"])

Release inventory at that moment:

    v0.0.42   2026-07-30T07:57Z   darwin only  <- latest, no linux asset
    v0.0.41   2026-07-30T07:27Z   HAS linux
    v0.0.40   2026-07-30T06:45Z   HAS linux
    v0.0.39   2026-07-30T05:56Z   HAS linux

So helsinki was not blocked by a broken build. It was blocked by a policy of only ever considering the newest tag. A usable Linux binary existed 30 minutes older and was ignored.

WHY THIS IS NOT A RARE EDGE CASE

Multi-platform releases do not publish atomically. Per-platform jobs finish at different times, and some fail or get starved independently: on this fleet, aarch64-linux jobs have been observed starved on a permanently busy runner (bd-893ff0), and a separate defect fails an aarch64-linux release job after the binary has already published (bd-8b49a7). Caravan cut five releases in two hours on the day this was observed. With that cadence, the window where "latest" is platform-incomplete is not an anomaly; it is a routine state, and every Linux node hits it.

The failure is also worst where it matters most. Whichever platform is slowest or flakiest to build is exactly the platform whose nodes can never self-update, because "latest" is perpetually ahead of their last usable asset.

WANTED

Resolve self-update against "the newest release carrying an asset for THIS platform", not "the newest release". Concretely:

- Walk releases newest-first and select the first one with a matching asset, within a bounded lookback.
- Report the choice explicitly: "updating to v0.0.41 (v0.0.42 has no x86_64-linux asset)". Silently taking an older version would be its own problem; the point is to proceed while saying why.
- Keep a bounded search. If no release within, say, the last N carries a matching asset, that IS a real failure and should say so - the platform's build pipeline is broken, which is a different and more serious condition than one late tag.
- Consider whether a release that is platform-incomplete should be marked as such, so consumers can distinguish "still publishing" from "this platform failed".

This belongs in the shared updatable-cli behaviour rather than in cara specifically, since any tool using it has the same exposure.

IMPACT IS LARGER THAN A VERSION LAG. THIS BUG IS CURRENTLY KEEPING A MERGE QUEUE BROKEN.

Measured on helsinki, 2026-07-30 ~11:45Z:

    which cara            /home/harry/.local/bin/cara   (a real binary, exactly what self-update maintains)
    cara --version        0.0.27

The caravan fixes that make the queue function are in v0.0.30/31 - notably a producer/consumer problem-kind mismatch that left the head-of-line guard silently dead since 0.0.27, with all tests green because the unit test injected the old kind by hand.

So helsinki is running the LAST version before the fix, and self-update cannot advance it because the newest release is platform-incomplete for x86_64-linux.

THE CAUSAL CHAIN, END TO END:

    self-update refuses to fall back to the newest release WITH a linux asset
      -> helsinki stays on cara 0.0.27
      -> 0.0.27 predates the head-of-line fix
      -> the merge queue cannot function correctly on the node that hosts it
      -> no caravan forms

Context on how much this cost: a caravan had never once formed on cacophony until 2026-07-30, and days of correct diagnosis by three separate agents went into code nobody was running (bd-ee4a2d). When one finally formed, it was against a runtime built ad-hoc for verification rather than the installed binary.

Right now there are two CLEAN candidate PRs on cacophony and no caravan, on a node whose cara predates the fix.

That reframes the priority. This is not "a node is one version behind". It is "the node that hosts the merge queue cannot run a working merge queue, and the mechanism that would fix it refuses to act because an unrelated platform's build was late".

Note also the compounding property already recorded on this bead: whichever platform is slowest or flakiest to build is exactly the platform whose nodes can never self-update. helsinki is x86_64-linux, and x86_64-linux is the platform observed being starved on a permanently busy runner (bd-893ff0) and failing a release job after the binary already published (bd-8b49a7).

title: the windows CI job's comment still cites the dead azure-ephemeral allowlist premise
description:
The `windows` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml carries the same dead premise that bd-a5b044
just removed from the `check` job, one job below it:

    windows:
      name: Windows compile + test
      # updatable-cli is not yet in collective's self-hosted Windows runner allowlist.
      # Use the native MSVC GitHub runner now; switch to [self-hosted, windows] once it is.
      runs-on: windows-latest

That comment tells the next reader that moving this job to self-hosted is gated on being added
to a shared pool's allowlist. It is not, and never was.

VERIFIED, not inferred (`gh api repos/harryaskham/updatable-cli/actions/runners`, 2026-07-30):
updatable-cli has 14 runners registered DIRECTLY on the repository, all `online`, including
six Windows runners:

    updatable-cli-win-ms-dev     online   [self-hosted, X64, Windows]
    updatable-cli-win-ms-dev-2   online   [self-hosted, X64, Windows]
    updatable-cli-win-ms-dev-3   online   [self-hosted, X64, Windows]
    updatable-cli-win-ms-dev-4   online   [self-hosted, X64, Windows]
    updatable-cli-win-ms-dev-5   online   [self-hosted, X64, Windows]
    updatable-cli-win-ms-dev-6   online   [self-hosted, X64, Windows]

No allowlist is involved for a repo-level runner. The stated blocker does not exist.

This is the same class of defect as bd-ab07b8 and bd-59aa1f: a false premise in a comment,
which outlives the code around it because the next reader acts on it instead of re-deriving
it. It is exactly what kept the `check` job queued for 17 days against a pool it did not need
while this repo's own runners sat idle.

SCOPE - what this bead does and deliberately does NOT claim:

DO fix the comment so it states what is true: the job runs on GitHub-hosted windows-latest,
this repo has its own self-hosted Windows runners, and no allowlist gates a move.

DO NOT switch `runs-on` as part of this. Whether those runners can actually run this job is
UNVERIFIED. Their labels are `[self-hosted, X64, Windows]` with no `nix`, and the job uses
`dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` plus an assertion on `host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; whether
rustup and an MSVC toolchain are present and working there has not been tested. The bd-a5b044
`actions/cache` failure is the cautionary case - a step that worked on GitHub-hosted runners
died immediately on the Nix-packaged self-hosted ones because they lack a node20 external.

Also note the current lane is NOT broken: windows-latest is green on every commit in ~72s and
is presently the only enforced gate for `#[cfg(windows)]` code. So a switch is an optional
improvement (runner consistency, no GitHub-hosted minutes), not a repair, and it should be
decided on evidence from an actual trial rather than on the assumption that self-hosted must
be better.

Record the switch as an open option in the comment; do not perform it blind.
creator: ms-dev-4:updatable-cli:ms-dev-4-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-md4-0

title: status cannot tell you the maintained binary is shadowed by an older copy earlier in PATH
description:
`UpdateStatus` reports the path this crate MAINTAINS. It does not report whether that path is the one a shell would actually run. On a machine where an older copy of the tool sits earlier in PATH, self-update can be working perfectly, report success, and change nothing about what the operator invokes.

Observed on ms-dev-3 while closing out bd-0497f6, checking the installed version rather than the dispatch receipt:

    ~/.local/bin/cara       cara 0.0.26   <- what updatable-cli maintains (mtime Jul 29 00:57)
    ~/.cargo/bin/cara       cara 0.0.22   <- what `cara` actually resolves to (mtime Jul 28)
    ~/.nix-profile/bin/cara cara 0.0.22   -> /nix/store/...caravan-0.0.22/bin/cara

    PATH position 4  : ~/.cargo/bin      <- wins
    PATH position 10 : ~/.local/bin

So `cara --version` reports 0.0.22 while the binary this crate manages is 0.0.26, and a
`cara status` built on `current_status()` would print `installed_path: ~/.local/bin/cara`
next to a `current_version` taken from the RUNNING 0.0.22 image — two different binaries
reported as one. Latest release is 0.0.51.

This is the same shape as the bug this project fixed today: a mechanism that is healthy in
itself, defeated silently by something just outside it, with the failure invisible on the
surface that is supposed to report health. The README already documents the requirement —
"Service modules that prefer the local binary can simply prepend $HOME/.local/bin to PATH" —
which makes it a documented precondition that nothing checks and nothing reports.

WANTED

Report the discrepancy rather than requiring the operator to notice it:

- Resolve the tool name against PATH (first match, honoring the platform's executable
  extension) and compare it to `installed_binary_path()`.
- Add to `UpdateStatus` something like `path_resolved: Option<String>` plus
  `shadowed: bool`, so `<tool> status` can say: "installed 0.0.26 at ~/.local/bin/cara, but
  `cara` on PATH resolves to ~/.cargo/bin/cara — this install is shadowed".
- Consider the same warning on the `run_update` outcome, since promoting a binary nobody
  will execute is a successful no-op from the user's point of view. That is the case worth
  catching: it reports success and changes nothing.
- Keep it non-fatal and read-only. Resolving PATH must never fail an update; this is
  reporting, not enforcement, and the crate must not start rewriting anyone's PATH.

Note it is genuinely ambiguous which binary "should" win — a nix-profile or cargo-installed
copy may be deliberate on some hosts. That is an argument for reporting it clearly, not for
picking a side.

SEPARATE, UNEXPLAINED, NOT PART OF THIS BEAD: the maintained binary is itself 25 releases
behind (0.0.26 vs 0.0.51, with 0.0.49/50/51 all published today). Whether that is because
nothing invokes self-update on this node, or because it is failing, I did not determine and
am deliberately not asserting. Worth someone checking, since it would mean the mechanism is
idle rather than merely shadowed.

title: Add integration test for updatable-cli promote_next / maybe_apply_staged_update
description: promote_next and maybe_apply_staged_update perform the on-disk rename/re-exec promotion contract (the riskiest part touching real binaries), but src/lib.rs only tests current_status. A tempdir-based test that stages a fake <tool>_next, calls promote_next, and asserts the installed binary appears with 0755 perms (and that promote_next returns None when nothing is staged) would lock in the promotion semantics. Filed via reflect-session/cacophony-bead-scope from updatable-cli scaffold review (no active bead; queue empty).

title: Have register_update_tool publish MCP output schemas
description: Discovered during Caravan bd-af5c3d SPEC/CLI/MCP parity audit: updatable-cli's UpdateStatus, LatestReleaseInfo, and UpdateOutcome already derive JsonSchema, but register_update_tool uses add_typed_tool rather than add_typed_tool_with_output_schema. Consequently self_update_status/check/run metadata omit outputSchema and hosts must duplicate the registrar to satisfy a fully typed MCP contract. Switch the registrar and add metadata tests; preserve names and handlers.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-1

title: Install a downloaded release to an explicit target directory
description:
Today the updater only replaces the currently running executable in place. That leaves consumers with no first-party option when the running binary is immutable or package-managed, for example /nix/store/...-caravan-0.0.7/bin/cara, where an in-place write is impossible and would corrupt the store closure if it somehow succeeded.

Add a generic capability: resolve and download the selected release asset, verify its digest, and install it to an explicit caller-supplied target directory instead of over the current executable. Preserve every existing check (version resolution, asset selection, digest verification, executable permissions, atomic replace within the target directory).

Deliberate scope boundary: this crate must NOT decide where installing is acceptable. It performs no package-manager detection, no PATH-precedence policy, and no store protection. It takes an explicit destination and reports exactly what it wrote, including resolved source asset, version, destination path, and artifact hash. Callers own policy.

Consumer counterpart is a Caravan bead that adds the forced self-update path: it refuses store and Homebrew destinations outright, requires the destination to precede the package-managed binary in PATH, and emits a loud shadowing receipt. File that Caravan bead as the dependent so ordering is explicit.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Make updatable-cli compile and stage safely on Windows
description:
Ring's native Windows MIDI/Ableton build is blocked because updatable-cli is explicitly Unix-only: it uses std::os::unix PermissionsExt/CommandExt, assumes binaries named without `.exe`, and release_target only maps linux/darwin. Ring imports Updater types across main/update/MCP/TUI, so target-gating one call is insufficient.

Add Windows portability without weakening Unix behavior:
- Compile the full crate/tests for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.
- cfg-gate executable permissions and exec replacement; preserve current atomic staged-update behavior on Unix.
- Define safe Windows staged/current executable naming (`tool.exe`, `tool_next.exe`) and a promotion strategy compatible with Windows locking. If replacing a running exe cannot be made safe in this slice, make startup promotion an explicit nonfatal/no-op with actionable status rather than failing compilation or corrupting the current binary.
- Extend release_target / Tendril-style asset naming with a documented canonical Windows suffix (coordinate with ring's planned `x86_64-windows` asset).
- Keep Updater, MCP registration, current_status, check_latest, and download/checksum APIs usable by Windows callers.
- Add cfg-specific unit tests and a Windows CI compile/test job on an existing self-hosted Windows runner if the project has one.
- Document host integration expectations for downstream CLIs.

Downstream: ring-mods bd-af3e23 needs this on main to ship a native Windows Ring MIDI bridge for Harry's Ableton Live test.
creator: aurora:ring-mods:aurora-ring-mods-ring-dev-aur-0

title: Rework CI to use a Nix devshell for the toolchain (azure-ephemeral runners)
description:
Operator directive (2026-06-28): the azure-ephemeral runners are Nix-based, so prebuilt-toolchain actions (dtolnay/rust-toolchain downloads a rustc that won't run under NixOS's linker) fail with "missing toolchain". Rework CI to obtain the toolchain from a Nix devshell instead of a runner image / rustup download.

updatable-cli has no flake today. Add a minimal flake.nix exposing a default devShell with the Rust toolchain (cargo, rustc, rustfmt, clippy) — the crate is pure-Rust (rustls TLS, miniz flate2), so no system libs needed. Rework .github/workflows/ci.yml: drop the dtolnay/rust-toolchain step and run each check via `nix develop --command cargo ...` (runners have Nix+flakes preinstalled). Keep checkout + cargo cache.

Acceptance: flake.nix + flake.lock committed; `nix develop --command cargo fmt --all --check / clippy --all-targets -D warnings / test` all pass locally; ci.yml uses nix develop. Note: updatable-cli still needs adding to the runner pool `repos` allowlist (separate operator action) before CI actually runs there.
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Document all public items and enforce with #![warn(missing_docs)]
description:
A `RUSTFLAGS="-W missing_docs" cargo build` shows 39 undocumented public items in src/lib.rs (7 structs, 22 struct fields, 8 methods, 2 associated functions), including the public result types (UpdateStatus, LatestReleaseInfo, UpdateOutcome, AssetNames) and several Updater methods (new, config, current_status, check_latest, stage_next, run_update) and EmptyArgs/UpdateError. For a crate that ships full crates.io publishing metadata, this leaves a sparse docs.rs page.

Add `#![warn(missing_docs)]` at the crate root and write a concise doc comment for every public item so the lint is satisfied. Because CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, this also enforces documentation on all future public items (new undocumented pub items will fail CI).

Acceptance: `RUSTFLAGS="-W missing_docs" cargo build` is clean (0 missing-doc warnings); cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + test (22 unit + 2 doc-tests) stay green; cargo doc --no-deps builds clean. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Add CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog) for the publish-intended crate
description:
updatable-cli ships with full crates.io publishing metadata (description, license, keywords, categories, repository, homepage) but has no CHANGELOG.md. For a reusable crate intended to be embedded across the CLI suite, a changelog is standard, expected documentation so adopters can see what changed between versions.

State: version 0.1.0, no git tags, no GitHub releases (pre-first-release), so all current work belongs under an Unreleased / 0.1.0 section.

Add a CHANGELOG.md following the Keep a Changelog convention with an Unreleased (toward 0.1.0) section summarizing the implemented surface, grouped Added/Changed:
- Updater core: current_status, check_latest, stage_next (sha256-verified), promote_next, run_update; maybe_apply_staged_update re-exec; register_update_tool MCP surface (self_update_status/check/run); Tendril-style asset strategy + Custom; release_target.
- Private-repo support: github_token, gh_account / gh_token_fallback, bearer dropped on cross-host redirect (bd-d3e3c8).
- Repo hygiene + CI workflow (bd-c381de); mock-HTTP + integration tests (bd-378b81, bd-247d71).
- Unix-only support made explicit; dead non-unix branch removed (bd-3b5d1c).
- Friendlier check_latest errors for 404 no-releases and 403/429 rate-limit (bd-d7a396).

Acceptance: CHANGELOG.md present, accurate, Keep-a-Changelog format; cargo fmt/clippy/test still green (docs-only, no code impact). Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: Make Unix-only platform support explicit; remove dead #[cfg(not(unix))] exec_replace branch
description:
Portability inconsistency in src/lib.rs.

Current state:
- Module unconditionally does `use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;` (top of lib.rs) and calls `set_mode(...)` in `set_executable` and tests. These are Unix-only APIs; `std::os::unix` does not exist on Windows, so the crate cannot compile on non-Unix targets.
- `release_target()` only maps linux->linux and macos->darwin, and bails on any other OS. So even at runtime only Linux/macOS are supported.
- Despite that, `exec_replace` has a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` fallback (spawn + exit) alongside the `#[cfg(unix)]` `CommandExt::exec` path. Because the unconditional unix import already prevents non-unix compilation, the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` branch is unreachable/dead code and never builds.

Net: the crate is effectively Unix-only (Linux/macOS), but the dead non-unix branch and the cfg gating imply cross-platform intent that does not hold. For a reusable crate published with full crates.io metadata, this is misleading.

Recommended minimal fix (commit to Unix-only honestly):
- Remove the dead `#[cfg(not(unix))]` exec_replace fn and the now-redundant `#[cfg(unix)]` gate on the remaining definition, making exec_replace a plain Unix fn consistent with the rest of the module.
- Add an explicit "Platform support: Unix (Linux/macOS) only" note to the crate-level doc comment and the README.

Optional larger follow-up (defer unless there is demand): add real Windows support — cfg-gate the unix imports, provide a Windows set_executable no-op, and add a Windows release_target arm plus a zip-based asset strategy. Not in scope for this bead.

Acceptance: crate still builds + cargo test/clippy/fmt pass; no dead non-unix branch remains; docs/README state Unix-only support. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli (board was empty).
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Rollback support: keep <tool>_prev and auto-restore on bad update
description: Idea (drafted while idle): rollback safety for self-update. On promote_next, keep the outgoing binary as <tool>_prev; add Updater::rollback() to restore it. Also make maybe_apply_staged_update auto-rollback to <tool>_prev if the freshly promoted binary fails to re-exec / exits nonzero immediately, so a bad release can't brick the tool. Pure-Unix, testable. Complements the existing atomic promote.
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Update mcp-cli dependency to renamed mcp-cli-core package
description:
Current main depends on `mcp-cli = { git = "https://github.com/harryaskham/mcp-cli", branch = "main" }`, but mcp-cli main renamed the package to `mcp-cli-core` while retaining the Rust library name. Fresh `cargo metadata` now fails with `no matching package named mcp-cli found`. Change the dependency to `mcp-cli = { package = "mcp-cli-core", ..., rev = <reviewed pin> }`, refresh the lock, and retain API compatibility. Discovered while scaffolding finance bd-8cbdcf.

Implemented and published as https://github.com/harryaskham/updatable-cli/pull/1 at head f3714b64055a26ed946a9b2ff8c1db1a3eb2a706. Validation: rustfmt; 50 unit tests; 2 doctests. Awaiting merge/CI; do not close before confirmed mainline landing.
creator: ms-mac:updatable-cli:harryaskham

title: Authenticate private GitHub release asset downloads through API
description: Caravan v0.0.1 private-repository live self-update proof: release metadata succeeds with gh-token fallback, but run then downloads `browser_download_url` at `https://github.com/harryaskham/caravan/releases/download/v0.0.1/cara-0.0.1-aarch64-darwin.tar.gz` and receives HTTP 404 even with GH_TOKEN. Exact 0.0.0 fixture binary, temp HOME, published assets/checksums; metadata/check is green. GitHub private assets require authenticated `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/assets/{asset_id}` with `Accept: application/octet-stream`, following the signed redirect without forwarding Authorization cross-origin. Preserve public browser URL behavior, checksum verification, token secrecy, and redirect auth stripping. Add mock tests for private API asset IDs, 302 signed redirects, public assets, missing token 404 guidance, and checksum leg. title: [operator-action] Add updatable-cli to azure-ephemeral runner pool repos allowlist
description:
updatable-cli's CI is fully migrated to the azure-ephemeral runners (runs-on [self-hosted, azure-ephemeral] + Nix devshell toolchain, validated locally, landed 2ec7001), but updatable-cli is NOT in the runner pool's repos allowlist — so its CI jobs queue indefinitely with no runner (verified: pushes 28330594095, 28334705783 stuck queued 3-4h+). Per the directive, only x86/Linux pure build/test (no secrets/tailnet), so once added it runs clean.

OPERATOR ACTION: append `updatable-cli` to `repos` in sandbox/ops/terraform/runners.nix (cacophony/collective repo) and redeploy. This is outside updatable-cli worker scope. Pool currently covers: collective, cacophony, agent-utils, android-utils, apple-utils, tendril, omni-cli, ring-mods, kittui, midi2hid — not updatable-cli. Tracking the remaining gate so it isn't lost in chat.

UPDATE (2026-07-01, per bd-f35766 deploy broadcast): the azure-ephemeral runner pool now has a shared Azure Files build-cache at /mnt/build-cache (shared CARGO_HOME + per-runner scratch, cleaned on exit); all 11 runners intact. DEPLOY-PATH CLARIFICATION for this operator-action: sandbox CI workflows (sandbox-terraform.yml, runner-image.yml) have NO Azure OIDC federation and fail at Azure Login; sandbox-terraform.yml is now plan-only. So after appending updatable-cli to repos in sandbox/ops/terraform/runners.nix, the redeploy must be applied MANUALLY via sandbox/deploy.sh (local az + real secrets), NOT by pushing and expecting CI to apply it. Still operator/ops scope; noting the corrected apply path so the allowlist change is not pushed-and-forgotten. Caveat: SMB build-cache does not host /nix, so it does not fix nix-build OOM (bd-256755 tracks binary-cache substitution); updatable-cli CI is pure x86 build/test per the migration, so this cache is a net win for it.

CLARIFICATION (2026-07-02, re bd-f35766 fleet CI regression): the SMB-CARGO_HOME rustup-hardlink failure breaking azure rust repos does NOT affect updatable-cli. Verified in this checkout: ci.yml provisions the toolchain via `nix develop --command cargo ...` from the flake devShells.default (nixpkgs cargo+rustc), NOT dtolnay/rust-toolchain+rustup, so there is no rustup toolchain-install that would hardlink into /mnt/build-cache/cargo-home. The workflow also caches default ~/.cargo via actions/cache and references neither /mnt/build-cache nor CARGO_HOME. Net: this regression is NOT a reason to defer the runner-allowlist gate for updatable-cli — its CI is immune by construction. (Supersedes the earlier "net win" phrasing: accurate statement is "immune to the rustup-link breakage; toolchain is nixpkgs via devshell".)

TRIAGE 2026-07-30 (ms-dev-4, not claiming — this remains operator-action). Confirming the
gate is STILL open one month on, with fresh evidence, and quantifying an impact that is not
yet recorded here and that changes how workers should validate this repo.

STILL BLOCKED. Every one of today's four pushes queued with no runner:

    run 30558426176  19fa5dd  15:47Z  fmt + clippy + test: QUEUED
    run 30558098953  d690937  15:43Z  fmt + clippy + test: QUEUED
    run 30557420498  d3d2929  15:35Z  fmt + clippy + test: QUEUED
    run 30556307296  d2533df  15:21Z  fmt + clippy + test: QUEUED

Those four commits are the bd-0497f6 / bd-323a05 / bd-ab07b8 / bd-d52a2a work landed today.
So the allowlist entry described in this bead has still not been applied, and the queue is
now accumulating runs that will never start. The last `check` job to actually complete was
2026-07-18 (run 29632764253); everything since has queued.

NEW AND IMPORTANT: the Windows job is NOT affected, and it passes.

    Windows compile + test: completed/SUCCESS   on all four runs above

`windows` uses `runs-on: windows-latest` (a GitHub-hosted runner), so it is outside the
self-hosted pool and runs normally. This is worth recording because it means the repo is not
unvalidated — it is HALF validated, in a way that is easy to misread in either direction:

  - Windows-specific code IS covered by hosted CI. Concretely, today's `install_binary`
    move-aside path and the `atomic_write` pre-delete removal are both Windows-only code that
    no agent here can compile locally (no rustup, no MSVC target in the devshell), and both
    were validated by that job.
  - Linux fmt/clippy/test is covered by NOTHING hosted. The only thing standing behind the
    Linux side of every commit landed today is each agent's local
    `nix develop --command cargo fmt --all --check / clippy --all-targets -D warnings / test`.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE CI SLOWDOWN. The shared worker profile says hosted CI owns final
validation and tells workers NOT to re-run a broad local gate that CI will immediately
repeat. On this repo that assumption is currently FALSE for the Linux job: there is no
hosted repeat, so an agent following the general guidance would land Linux-side changes with
no fmt/clippy/test coverage at all. Until the allowlist lands, updatable-cli workers should
keep running the full local triple before reintegrating, and treat it as the real gate rather
than a redundant pre-check.

That is a worker-facing behavioural consequence, so it is stated here rather than left to be
rediscovered. I have also broadcast it to the project.

NO CHANGE to the operator action itself. It is still: append `updatable-cli` to `repos` in
sandbox/ops/terraform/runners.nix and apply MANUALLY via sandbox/deploy.sh per the 2026-07-01
clarification, since sandbox-terraform.yml is plan-only with no Azure OIDC. The 2026-07-02
clarification also still holds — this repo's toolchain comes from the flake devshell, not
rustup, so the SMB-CARGO_HOME hardlink regression is not a reason to defer.

Worth deciding as part of applying it: whether to cancel the accumulated queued runs, since
four (and counting) will otherwise sit queued forever and may occupy pool scheduling slots
once the repo IS allowlisted.

EVIDENCE 2026-07-30 (ms-dev-3, not claiming — still operator-action): this gate is no longer a
migration leftover. The repo's primary validation lane has been DARK for 17 days, and six
commits landed into it today.

Measured with `gh run list/view --repo harryaskham/updatable-cli`:

    30561846758  bd-59aa1f   queued   (never started)
    30560212586  bd-1eca98   queued
    30558426176  bd-d52a2a   queued
    30558098953  bd-ab07b8   queued
    30557420498  bd-323a05   queued
    30556307296  bd-0497f6   queued   ~1h11m and counting

Per-job breakdown of 30556307296 is the important part, because the two jobs have different
fates and the run-level status hides it:

    ✓ Windows compile + test    1m18s   runs-on: windows-latest        (GitHub-hosted)
    * fmt + clippy + test       queued  runs-on: [self-hosted, azure-ephemeral]

So the Windows lane IS being enforced on every commit. The Unix lane — `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the ENTIRE `cargo test` suite — is not
running at all, because `[self-hosted, azure-ephemeral]` has no runner that accepts this repo.
That is exactly the allowlist gap this bead tracks.

History confirms it is chronic rather than a today problem:

    29240658472  2026-07-13   ✓ fmt + clippy + test  3m36s     <- last successful Unix run
    29237950144  2026-07-13   ✓ fmt + clippy + test  3m27s
    29632764253  2026-07-18   X fmt + clippy + test  24h0m1s   <- timed out, never picked up
    28334705783  2026-06-28   X fmt + clippy + test  24h0m1s

Note the failure shape: the job does not fail fast, it sits for 24 hours and is then cancelled
by timeout. A reader skimming `gh run list` sees "cancelled" and reads infrastructure flake,
not "this repo has no runner".

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALLED CI MIGRATION

Managed workers here operate under a merge-queue policy that says hosted CI owns final
test/lint validation and that agents should NOT re-run that gate locally. For this repo's
Unix lane that premise is currently false. Today it happened to be harmless — both agents on
this project ran `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the full suite
locally before every reintegration, so all six commits are in fact validated. But they are
validated by convention, not by enforcement. The first worker that follows the merge-queue
policy literally and skips local validation lands unvalidated code into main, and the signal
that would have caught it sits queued for 24 hours and then reports "cancelled".

The exposure is asymmetric in the same way the bug this project fixed today was: the lane that
is silently unenforced is the lane carrying rustfmt, clippy-as-error, and 100% of the test
suite, while the lane that works covers compile+test on the platform nobody develops on.

SUGGESTED, in preference order (all operator/ops scope, none actionable from a worker):

1. Land the allowlist change this bead already describes: append `updatable-cli` to `repos` in
   sandbox/ops/terraform/runners.nix and apply MANUALLY via sandbox/deploy.sh per the
   2026-07-01 clarification (sandbox-terraform.yml is plan-only, no Azure OIDC).
2. If that is not imminent, consider an interim `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` for the `check` job so
   the Unix lane is enforced by SOMETHING today. It needs a Nix install step, since the job
   body is `nix develop --command ...` and GitHub-hosted images have no Nix. Strictly worse
   than the self-hosted pool (no shared build cache) but strictly better than dark.
3. If neither is imminent, the honest move is to tell workers on this project that local
   validation is mandatory rather than discouraged, since that is the only gate that exists.

Priority raised P2 -> P1 on that basis: not because the allowlist is more urgent in itself, but
because "no Unix CI" is currently invisible and is being actively relied upon.

CORRECTION 2026-07-30 (ms-dev-3, same author as the evidence block above, ~20 minutes later).
My claim that the Unix lane carries "100% of the test suite" was WRONG. Struck.

Verified in .github/workflows/ci.yml rather than inferred from the job name — the last step of
the `windows` job is:

    - name: Compile and test all targets
      run: |
        cargo test --all-targets
        cargo test --doc

So the Windows lane runs the whole suite plus doctests on every commit, in ~80 seconds, not
merely a compile. Counted against the current tree: 53 tests, of which 1 is `#[cfg(unix)]`
(promote_next_moves_staged_binary_and_marks_executable) and 3 are `#[cfg(windows)]`.

CORRECTED GAP:

    cargo fmt --all --check                    NOT enforced anywhere
    clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings        NOT enforced anywhere
    1 of 53 tests (unix chmod/rename)          NOT enforced anywhere
    ALL #[cfg(unix)] production code           NEVER COMPILED in CI (see below)
    the other 52 tests + doctests              enforced every commit, on Windows

The credit for catching this is ms-dev-4's; they checked the workflow body while I had reasoned
from the job name. That makes this the fourth unverified claim to land in a durable record on
this project today, and mine, in the very block arguing the record must be accurate.

ONE ADDITION THE CORRECTION DOES NOT COVER, which keeps this more than a lint gap:

No Linux or macOS COMPILATION happens in CI at all. The only lane that runs builds for
x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, so every `#[cfg(unix)]` block in src/lib.rs is excluded from the build
entirely — currently the PermissionsExt import, the Unix `set_executable` (chmod 0755), and the
`exec`-based re-exec used by maybe_apply_staged_update. A change that fails to COMPILE on Linux,
or that breaks Unix-only logic, passes CI today. For a crate whose primary consumers are Linux
and macOS CLIs, and whose default install path is $HOME/.local/bin, that is the more serious
half of the remaining hole — bigger than the single cfg(unix) test it also hides.

INTERIM OPTION 2 IS CHEAPER THAN I DESCRIBED, and closes more than I claimed.

I said it would need a Nix install step to reproduce this repo's devshell. It does not. fmt and
clippy need a rustfmt/clippy toolchain, not the devshell (ms-dev-4's point), and the same
ubuntu-latest job can also run the test suite. So:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest + dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable (rustfmt, clippy)
      cargo fmt --all --check                  -> closes the fmt gap
      cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings -> closes the clippy gap AND compiles for Linux
      cargo test                                -> closes the last cfg(unix) test

That is well under a minute, has no allowlist dependency, and closes every item above. The
residual reason to still want the allowlist is toolchain parity: the devshell pins a nixpkgs
Rust, so a stable-channel clippy can differ in its lint set from what agents run locally. That
is a real but much smaller concern than having no Unix lint or Unix compilation at all, and it
is the correct thing for the allowlist to fix rather than a prerequisite for having any gate.

Net: the operator choice presented from this bead understated option 2's value and overstated
its cost. If option 2 is selected I will implement the version above, not the Nix one.

UPDATE 2026-07-30 (ms-dev-3): the urgency I added an hour ago is RESOLVED, and this bead may now
be obsolete. Priority returned P1 -> P2 by the same author who raised it.

The operator resolved choice-019fb3e1 with "self-hosted only, not azure-ephemeral". Acting on
that revealed the premise error underneath this whole bead: updatable-cli did not need to be
added to any shared pool, because it already has 14 self-hosted runners registered directly on
the repo, all online, and had throughout — 7 Linux with self-hosted+nix+x86_64-linux+nixos, 1
macOS, 6 Windows. The `check` job was asking for a label pair (`azure-ephemeral`) that none of
them carries, so it queued against a pool it did not need while its own runners sat idle.

Fixed under bd-a5b044, landed 6b7ed03 + 267dbb3, and VERIFIED GREEN rather than assumed:

    run 30563226049   ✓ fmt + clippy + test        53s   <- first Unix success since 2026-07-13
                      ✓ Windows compile + test   1m12s

The first attempt (6b7ed03) is worth recording because it failed for a second, unrelated reason
that this bead's original framing would also have hit: `actions/cache@v4` died in 9s with "The
template is not valid ... externals/node20/bin/node ... No such file or directory". The cache
key called `hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock')`, and hashFiles is evaluated by spawning a node20
external the Nix-packaged runner does not ship. That step was additionally hashing a file this
crate intentionally does not track, and existed only to serve EPHEMERAL runners that start
empty. Removed in 267dbb3 with all three reasons recorded in the workflow.

WHAT IS LEFT OF THIS BEAD

Very little, and possibly nothing:

- The Unix lane is enforced again — fmt, clippy -D warnings, the full suite, and the Linux
  COMPILATION that no lane was performing.
- The shared /mnt/build-cache that the azure-ephemeral pool offered is largely moot on these
  runners: they are persistent, with a stable workdir and HOME, so ~/.cargo and target/ survive
  between runs without any cache action at all. That is why removing the cache step cost
  nothing.

I have NOT closed it, because it is operator-action and not mine to close, and because there
may be a fleet-consistency reason to want this repo in the shared pool that is not visible from
here. But on the evidence above I would recommend closing it as obsolete: the gate it tracks is
no longer blocking anything, and the problem it described turned out to be a workflow label
error rather than a missing allowlist entry.

One thing worth keeping from it regardless of disposition: the failure shape. A `runs-on` label
that no runner carries does not fail fast. It queues for 24 hours and is then reported as
"cancelled", which reads as an infrastructure flake. That is how this survived 17 days and six
merges. The one-line check is now in the workflow:
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runners --jq '.runners[].labels[].name'`.

title: false Windows clock-granularity premise in the sidecar uniqueness comments (c36998d)
description:
A comment landed in c36998d (bd-1eca98) justifies the sidecar uniqueness counter with a
platform claim that is FALSE for the only Windows target this crate supports. The code is
correct; the stated reason is not.

The comment says `SystemTime`'s granularity is "far coarser on Windows", and the test says
the fixed-timestamp assertion "matters on Windows, where the clock is coarse enough to
repeat".

Checked against the actual toolchain rather than recalled:

    library/std/src/sys/pal/windows/time.rs:76
        pub fn now() -> SystemTime {
            unsafe {
                let mut t: SystemTime = mem::zeroed();
                c::GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime(&mut t.t);

`GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime` is documented by Microsoft as highest-available precision,
typically sub-microsecond — not the ~10-16ms class the comment implies. The coarse
`GetSystemTimeAsFileTime` path is real but it is the `*-win7-windows-*` compatibility
fallback, a target family this crate does not support: CI runs `windows-latest` and asserts
`host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, and `release_target_for` rejects every non-x86_64 Windows
arch. So the precise API is the only one in play here.

This is the same failure class as bd-ab07b8, which existed because a false premise about
Windows filesystem semantics sat unchallenged in a comment until someone checked it. Landing
a fresh false premise about Windows clock semantics into the SAME function, in the commit
that closed the audit prompted by that bead, is worth correcting promptly rather than leaving
for someone to disprove in six weeks.

The counter must stay. Its real justification is stronger and platform-independent:

1. `SystemTime` is NOT MONOTONIC. It can repeat or step backwards across an NTP adjustment
   regardless of resolution, so two calls can return the same reading on any platform,
   including Linux. Clock resolution was never the hazard; clock adjustment is.
2. Uniqueness should not rest on an argument about clocks at all. A counter is a guarantee.
   Any resolution claim is a probabilistic argument whose truth changes with target,
   toolchain and hardware — as this one just did.

WANTED

- Replace the granularity claims at src/lib.rs (the `windows_sidecar_path` comment and the
  two in `windows_sidecar_path_stays_beside_the_destination_and_is_unique`) with the
  non-monotonic justification. No behaviour change.
- While there: the 1000-iteration loop in that test cannot fail on a fine-grained clock and
  is kept only as a smoke check; make sure the comment says the fixed-timestamp assertion is
  the one carrying the guarantee, without attributing the difference to Windows.

Credit: identified by updatable-cli:ms-dev-3, who checked the std source path rather than
accepting the claim. Filed by ms-dev-4, who wrote the false comment and is taking the fix,
since it is a correction to a defect I introduced and landed rather than newly discovered
work.

title: Add a compile-checked rustdoc example for the MCP register_update_tool surface
description:
The crate's headline feature is the MCP integration (register_update_tool exposing self_update_status/check/run "for free"), but there is no compile-checked example of it — the README's MCP block is marked `rust,ignore` with placeholder types, so it never compiles, and the new crate-level Example only covers current_status.

Add a second crate-level rustdoc example (a real runnable doc-test, no network/IO) demonstrating the MCP surface:
- define a trivial host Ctx
- ToolRouter::<Ctx>::new()
- register_update_tool(&mut router, |_ctx| UpdaterConfig::new(tool, version, repo))
- assert the three tool names are registered via router.tool_metadata()

This mirrors the existing register_update_tool_registers_the_three_self_update_tools unit test but as documentation, so the primary public MCP entry point gains a compile- and run-checked example. mcp_cli is a normal dependency so it is available to doc-tests (same as anyhow in the current_status example).

Acceptance: cargo test runs the new doc-test (now 2 doc-tests) and it passes; fmt + clippy + the 22 unit tests stay green. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: CI check job targets a nonexistent azure-ephemeral label while 8 idle self-hosted nix runners are registered
description:
Operator direction, via resolution of choice-019fb3e1-4fac-7903-b9a6-17cef3dbf969: "self-hosted only, not azure-ephemeral".

The `check` job (fmt + clippy + test) targets `runs-on: [self-hosted, azure-ephemeral]`. No runner available to this repo carries the `azure-ephemeral` label, so the job has queued and been cancelled at the 24h timeout since 2026-07-13 — see the evidence block on bd-4fc064.

What makes this a one-line fix rather than an infrastructure request: this repo already has 14 self-hosted runners registered directly on it, all `"status":"online","busy":false` when checked (`gh api repos/harryaskham/updatable-cli/actions/runners`):

    8x Linux   labels: self-hosted, Linux, X64, nix, x86_64-linux, nixos, <node>
               (ms-dev, ms-dev-2..6, pocket4)
    1x macOS   labels: self-hosted, nix, macOS, ARM64, aarch64-darwin, ms-mac
    6x Windows labels: self-hosted, X64, Windows

They carry the `nix` and `nixos` labels, which is exactly what the job body needs — it runs `nix develop --command cargo ...` precisely because the runners ship no toolchain on PATH. So eight idle, online, Nix-capable runners were available this whole time and the job was asking for a label pair none of them has.

WANTED

Retarget the `check` job at the labels these runners actually carry, so the Unix lane is enforced again: fmt, clippy -D warnings, the full suite, and — the part that matters most — Linux COMPILATION, which no lane currently performs at all (the only working lane builds for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, so every `#[cfg(unix)]` block is excluded from every CI build today).

Deliberately NOT in scope, and why:

- The `windows` job stays on `windows-latest`. It works, in ~80s, on every commit, and it is
  currently the ONLY enforced lane. There are 6 self-hosted Windows runners registered, and
  the stale comment above that job says to switch "once it is" allowlisted — but whether those
  boxes have the MSVC build tools the job asserts (`host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) is not
  something I have verified. Switching the one working lane onto unverified runners to satisfy
  a general preference is how you end up with two dark lanes. Raised separately for the
  operator with that risk stated.
- No macOS lane is added here, though an aarch64-darwin runner is online and macOS is a
  supported platform that CI has never compiled. Worth its own bead rather than folding an
  untested new lane into a repair.

CORRECTION by the filer, before landing: the breakdown above says "8x Linux". It is SEVEN Linux
(ms-dev, ms-dev-2..6, pocket4) plus ONE macOS (ms-mac, aarch64-darwin). Eight runners carry the
`nix` label; seven can run this job. Counted exactly rather than eyeballed from the list:

    nix-labelled                      8
    nix + x86_64-linux (this job)     7
    nix + aarch64-darwin              1

Landing with `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, x86_64-linux]`, verified to match all seven online,
idle Linux runners. Chosen over `[self-hosted, Linux, X64]` because the job body is
`nix develop --command ...`, so `nix` is a real requirement and not a coincidence of the fleet;
and `x86_64-linux` rather than the node labels so the job is not pinned to one box.

Also recorded in the workflow itself: a label no runner carries does not fail fast, it queues
for 24h and reports "cancelled". That failure shape is why this went unnoticed for 17 days, so
the comment names it and gives the one-line `gh api ... /actions/runners` check.

title: atomic_write pre-deletes the Windows destination on a false premise about tempfile::persist
description:
`atomic_write` deletes the Windows destination before persisting, based on a claim about
`tempfile` that is not true for the version we depend on.

In `src/lib.rs`:

    // Windows rename/persist cannot replace an existing destination. This is only the
    // disposable staged path, never the installed executable, so removing an older staged
    // payload before persisting the newly checksum-verified one is safe.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    if destination.exists() {
        fs::remove_file(destination)...
    }
    tmp.persist(destination)

The premise is wrong. Verified against the resolved dependency (tempfile 3.27.0):

    src/file/mod.rs:205   imp::persist(&self.path, new_path.as_ref(), true)
    src/file/imp/windows.rs
                          if overwrite { flags |= MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING; }

So `NamedTempFile::persist` already passes `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING` and replaces an
existing destination on Windows. (`persist_noclobber` is the non-replacing variant.) The
pre-delete is therefore unnecessary, and it converts an atomic replace into a
delete-then-create with a window in which the staged path does not exist.

Impact is currently low and this is NOT a live bug: the only caller is the staged
`<tool>_next` path, which is disposable, and the failure mode is a re-download rather than
a corrupted install. Filing it because the stale comment is load-bearing for anyone
reasoning about Windows atomicity later, and the fix is a three-line deletion.

Wanted:
- Drop the `#[cfg(windows)]` pre-delete in `atomic_write` and let `persist` replace.
- Correct the comment to state what is actually true: `persist` replaces via
  MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING, but that still fails against a *locked* file, which is why the
  installed-executable paths deliberately do not use it.
- Keep a Windows test asserting a second `stage_next` over an existing `<tool>_next`
  succeeds (the existing `windows_atomic_write_replaces_only_the_staged_destination` test
  likely covers this once the pre-delete is gone).

Discovered while implementing bd-323a05 (install-to-explicit-target-dir), which needed a
correct answer to "can Windows persist replace an existing file?" before choosing its own
swap strategy. bd-323a05 does NOT use `atomic_write` for the installed binary; it renames
the incumbent aside first, because renaming a running .exe succeeds on Windows where
overwriting it does not.

title: Optional release signature verification (minisign/cosign/GPG) for downloaded binaries
description: Idea (drafted while idle): add release signature verification beyond the sha256 checksum. A self-updater that fetches+executes binaries is a supply-chain target; sha256 only proves integrity vs the published checksum, not authenticity. Add optional minisign/cosign/GPG signature verification of the release asset against a configured public key, gated by a verify policy in UpdaterConfig. Default off (back-compat), opt-in via with_signing_key(...). High value, self-contained, testable with mock keys. Sister to existing sha256 verify in stage_next.

title: Crate is not crates.io-publishable: mcp-cli git dependency has no version (cargo publish fails)
description:
updatable-cli ships full crates.io publishing metadata (description, license, keywords, categories, repository, homepage, readme) implying it is meant to be published, but `cargo publish --dry-run` FAILS:

  error: failed to verify manifest ... all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when publishing. dependency `mcp-cli` does not specify a version

Root cause: Cargo.toml depends on `mcp-cli = { git = "https://github.com/harryaskham/mcp-cli", branch = "main" }`. crates.io rejects git/path-only dependencies; every dependency (including optional ones) must carry a semver version that exists on crates.io.

Important: feature-gating / making mcp-cli optional does NOT bypass this — optional dependencies still require a version requirement at publish time. So the crate cannot be published to crates.io until mcp-cli itself is published to crates.io.

Options considered:
1. Publish mcp-cli to crates.io, then in updatable-cli pin a version (git for dev via [patch]).
2. Decide updatable-cli is intentionally NOT crates.io-published (git-only) and relax the publishing metadata.
3. Split the MCP surface into a separate crate so the core can publish without mcp-cli.

Verified via `cargo publish --dry-run`. Discovered during overnight in-lane review (node aurora).

DECISION (2026-06-23, operator via choice-019ef688, freeform "no crates.io, just idle"): option 2 — updatable-cli is intentionally NOT published to crates.io; it is consumed git-only across the CLI suite. The "not publishable" state is BY DESIGN, not a defect, so no fix is required. Optional non-urgent follow-up if ever desired: relax the crates.io publishing metadata (keywords/categories) so it doesn't imply crates.io intent. Deferred per operator "just idle"; left as draft for the operator to discard or action at leisure.

title: Private-repo support: attach token to asset downloads + optional gh-account token source
description:
Private-repo updates are only half-wired today. `UpdaterConfig.github_token` is sent as Authorization: Bearer only on the check_latest metadata request (lib.rs:224); the actual asset/checksum downloads in stage_next go through download_bytes/download_text which set User-Agent only and never attach the token. So even a correctly-authed caller cannot download a private release asset — it 404s. Confirmed bug, not caller misuse (kittui is wiring a stopgap).

Scope:
1. Thread the resolved token into asset + checksum downloads with redirect-safe handling that strips Authorization on cross-host redirects (GitHub -> signed S3 URL) so private downloads actually work.
2. Add an opt-in convenience for callers to source a token from the local gh CLI when none is set explicitly: new UpdaterConfig fields gh_account (Option<String>) and gh_token_fallback (bool), plus a gh_auth_token(account) helper running `gh auth token [--user <account>]`. github_token still wins; gh is only invoked when gh_account is set or gh_token_fallback is true, keeping existing public-repo behaviour and tests deterministic.
3. Builder helpers with_github_token/with_gh_account/with_gh_token_fallback and resolved_token().
4. Tests: auth header present on downloads when token set; auth stripped on cross-host redirect; resolved_token prefers explicit token without invoking gh.
5. README docs for private-repo + gh-account configuration.

Filed from updatable-cli dev session on operator request.

title: Add a compile-checked rustdoc example (doc-test) for the primary current_status path
description:
The crate currently has 0 doc-tests (cargo test reports "Doc-tests updatable_cli: running 0 tests"). The README usage examples are not compile-checked (the README is not wired in via doc(include_str!), and its runnable-looking blocks would hit the network), so the documented public-API usage can silently rot as the API evolves.

Add a single hermetic, network-free crate-level rustdoc example (a real runnable doc-test) to the module-level docs in src/lib.rs that exercises the primary status path:
- construct UpdaterConfig::new(tool, version, repo)
- set config.install_dir = Some(<temp path>) so the example never touches a real install dir
- call Updater::new(config).current_status()? and assert on tool/current_version and the derived installed/next paths

current_status performs no network or filesystem writes (only path computation + .exists() stats), so the doc-test is deterministic and fast. Use the `# Ok::<(), anyhow::Error>(())` trailing pattern (same as the README) so `?` works.

Acceptance: `cargo test` now runs >=1 doc-test and it passes; fmt + clippy + the existing 22 unit tests stay green. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: non-semver hosts can be silently downgraded when self-update falls back to an older platform-complete release
description:
Follow-up found while implementing bd-0497f6 (platform-aware release fallback, landed d2533df). Not a regression in the normal semver case; it is a pre-existing weakness that the new fallback makes reachable.

`Updater::is_newer` compares versions with semver when both sides parse, and otherwise degrades to plain string inequality:

    (Ok(latest), Ok(current)) => latest > current,
    _ => latest != self.config.current_version,

Before bd-0497f6 the only candidate was whatever `/releases/latest` returned, so "any different tag counts as newer" was a defensible fallback: the candidate really was the newest release. After bd-0497f6, selection can deliberately return an OLDER release (the newest one carrying this platform's assets). For a host whose `current_version` does not parse as semver — e.g. `nightly`, `2026-07-30-a`, or any date/channel scheme — the string-inequality branch then reports "newer" for a release that is actually older, and `run_update` will stage and promote a DOWNGRADE without saying so.

Concretely, with a non-semver versioning host:

    current:  nightly-b        (installed)
    releases: nightly-c        (newest, no asset for this platform -> skipped)
              nightly-a        (has this platform's asset -> selected)
    is_newer("nightly-a") == true   because "nightly-a" != "nightly-b"
    -> silently installs nightly-a over nightly-b

Semver hosts are unaffected: `is_newer` correctly returns false for an older selected version, `run_update` no-ops, and the note explains that a newer tag exists but publishes nothing for this platform (covered by `run_update_noop_note_explains_a_platform_incomplete_newer_release`).

WANTED

Make an unprovable ordering fail safe rather than fail silent. Sketch, not a prescription:

- Track whether the selected release was a fallback (`skipped_newer` is non-empty is already exactly that signal).
- When it IS a fallback and the two versions are not semver-comparable, do not treat "different string" as "newer". Either decline to stage with an explicit note ("cannot prove <selected> is newer than <current> without semver; refusing to install a possible downgrade"), or require an explicit opt-in on `UpdaterConfig`.
- Keep the existing non-semver behaviour for the non-fallback case, so nothing changes for hosts that are simply tracking the newest tag. `is_newer_handles_semver_ordering_and_non_semver_fallback` pins that contract and should keep passing.

Low priority: every in-suite consumer passes `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, which is semver, so no current host is exposed. It is filed because the failure mode (silent downgrade) is much worse than the trigger is likely, and because the guard is cheap once someone is in this code.

title: check_latest: friendlier errors for no-releases (404) and rate-limit (403/429)
description:
check_latest() in src/lib.rs propagates raw ureq errors instead of giving actionable messages for the two most common failure modes when polling GitHub releases:

- 404: the repo has no published releases yet (very common for a freshly set-up tool). Currently surfaces as a generic `GET <url>` ureq Status error.
- 403/429: GitHub API rate limiting (anonymous requests are limited to ~60/hr). Currently surfaces as a generic Status error with no hint that adding a token would fix it.

This is inconsistent with download_bytes(), which already maps `ureq::Error::Status(code, _)` to a clear `GET <url> returned HTTP <code>` message.

Fix: in check_latest, match on `request.call()`:
- 404 -> bail with "no published GitHub releases for <repo_slug> yet (GET <url> returned 404)"
- 403 | 429 -> bail with a message noting the request was rate-limited/forbidden and suggesting `UpdaterConfig::with_github_token` / `with_gh_token_fallback` to raise the limit
- other Status(code) -> "GET <url> returned HTTP <code>" (consistent with download_bytes)
- transport Err -> "GET <url>: <err>"

Add tests using a small std-only mock-HTTP helper that returns a custom status line (extend spawn_one_shot_http): one asserting the friendly no-releases message on 404, one asserting the rate-limit/token hint on 403.

Acceptance: cargo test/clippy/fmt pass; new tests cover 404 + 403 paths; behaviour unchanged on the success path. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: Install a downloaded release to an explicit target directory
description: Today the updater only replaces the currently running executable in place, so consumers have no first-party option when the running binary is immutable or package-managed (for example a /nix/store caravan binary), where an in-place write is impossible and would corrupt the store closure if it somehow succeeded. Add a generic capability: resolve and download the selected release asset, verify its digest, and install it to an explicit caller-supplied target directory instead of over the current executable, preserving version resolution, asset selection, digest verification, executable permissions, and atomic replace within that directory. Deliberate scope boundary: this crate must NOT decide where installing is acceptable - no package-manager detection, no PATH-precedence policy, no store protection. It takes an explicit destination and reports exactly what it wrote: resolved source asset, version, destination path, artifact hash. Callers own policy. Consumer counterpart is a Caravan bead adding the forced self-update path, which refuses store and Homebrew destinations, requires the destination to precede the package-managed binary in PATH, and emits a loud shadowing receipt.

title: Post-stage self-test: verify staged binary runs before promoting
description: Idea (drafted while idle): before promoting a staged binary, run it as a quick health check (e.g. <tool>_next --version) and only promote if it executes cleanly. Catches arch/ABI mismatches, corrupt downloads, and missing dynamic deps before they replace the working binary. Cheap, network-free, big safety win for run_update.
